name: anomaly_detector
intended_use: Flag pairing and session behaviour that is unlike typical legitimate use, for a second confirmation to the helpee or for human review.
out_of_scope_use: Must not block a session, ban an account, or be presented to any user as a finding of fraud. An anomaly score is a prompt to look, not a verdict.
training_data: 3000 synthetic normal observations plus 160 injected attacks across three scenarios, of which a majority are blended toward normal behaviour.
selection_criterion: PR-AUC and precision@k at review-queue capacities
limitations: Unsupervised: it detects unusualness, not malice. An unusual but legitimate helper will be flagged.
Attack scenarios are hand-specified; a novel pattern that mimics normal behaviour closely will be missed.
Legitimate behaviour drifts, so the threshold needs periodic refitting or it will alert on ordinary change.
ethical_considerations: Telling someone their family member looks suspicious is harmful when wrong, so the operating point favours precision and the output is advisory.
Scores must never be shown as accusations, and every alert carries its top contributing features so a human can judge it.
